newsitem.title: UK: Platinum above $400 in Europe at seven-month high.
newsitem.headline: Platinum above $400 in Europe at seven-month high.

text.p: Platinum prices rose above the $400 an ounce level in early European trading on Friday, the highest levels since the beginning of August last year.
Traders said the white metal's current strong trend was maintained, with spot prices indicated at $400.00/401.00, up from Thursday's late levels of $392.50/393.50.
Current firmness in platinum, as well as its sister metal palladium, reflects uncertainty over 1997 supply negotions between Russia and Japan.

There are also worries over a possible strike at Russia's Norilsk, with a key workers' meeting taking place over the weekend. Workers have threatened to strike at the complex -- a major producer of PGM's (platinum group metals) -- on March 15 over pay arrears.
Traders said prices had reached levels as high as $406 in earlier trading in the Far East on Friday before settling back to wait for the start of the key European and U.S. trading sessions.
Important price targets on the upside are $408.25, the May 1996 high, and then the crucial $410.75 area, the peak of April 1996.
